# Best Power Station + Solar Combos for an RV

The right combo depends mostly on one question: **do you want to run the roof air conditioner?** A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500W while running and spikes past 3,000W at startup. That pushes you into a much bigger, heavier, and pricier unit. [6](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

## Tier 1: Lights, fridge, laptop, CPAP (no AC)

**EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** (1,024Wh, 1,800W)
- Takes up to 1,000W of solar across two 500W inputs, the highest in its class.
- Recharges from the wall in about 56 minutes.
- Expandable to 5kWh.
- Weighs about 28 lb.

[7](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070Wh, 1,500W)
- Lighter at 23.8 lb and very simple to use.
- Solar input tops out at 400W, so two SolarSaga 200W panels max it out.
- Not expandable.

[7](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

## Tier 2: Full-time or multi-day boondocking (no AC)

**BLUETTI AC200L** (2,048Wh, 2,400W)
- Has a built-in 30A RV outlet.
- Takes 1,200W of solar.
- Heavy, at about 62 lb.

[6](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) [7](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**EcoFlow Delta 2 Max** (2,048Wh)
- Wall charges to 80% in about 43 minutes.
- Expandable to 6kWh.
- About $1,499.

[3](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti) [4](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)

## Tier 3: Running the roof AC

**EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**: the top RV pick in [6](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge.
- Expandable past 12kWh.
- Runs a roof AC for about 2.3 hours on one battery.
- Moving it is a two-person job.

**Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- 3,024Wh, 3,000W continuous, 6,000W surge.
- Enough to start a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit.

[6](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**ALLPOWERS R4000**: the budget option for this tier
- 3,456Wh LiFePO4 with an RV outlet.
- Takes 2,000W of solar, but only when panels are connected to all three inputs (650W max each).
- **Buy:** [https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)
- **Price:** $1,499. Code **EXTRA12** brings it to $1,319.12; it expires 2026-11-15, and the store takes one code per order.
- **Caveats:**
  - The "4,000W" in the title is the 230V rating. On US 120V outlets it's 3,600W.
  - It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb).
  - Sale items may not be returnable.
  - This is an affiliate deal page, so treat it as a store listing rather than a review.

[1](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)

## Choosing solar panels
- **Size panels to the station's solar input limit, not to its battery size.** Extra wattage beyond the limit is wasted. [5](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life) [7](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- **Check each input's voltage and current range** before wiring panels in series. [1](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) [7](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- **Plan on 300–400W of folding panels** to refill a mid-size unit in a sunny day. [6](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **Renogy's 200W foldable suitcase** is one suggested pairing. [4](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)

## Notes on the sources
- **Direct links:** The ALLPOWERS link is the only direct buy link in my search results. For the EcoFlow, Jackery, and Bluetti models, use the "check price" links in the cited guides or go to each brand's official US store.
- **Affiliate guides:** Every source here earns affiliate commissions.
- **Conflicting specs:** Some figures disagree between sources. For example, one says Bluetti leads on solar input [5](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life), while another says the older AC200P is capped at 700W with a 2-year warranty [3](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti).

**My take:** For most RVers who don't need AC, I'd pick the **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus with about 400–800W of panels**, or the **BLUETTI AC200L** if you want 2kWh and a 30A plug. If you need AC, I'd go with the **DELTA Pro 3**, or the **ALLPOWERS R4000** if price matters most.

What will you be running? I can size it more precisely.
